title: Smooth purity over an arbitrary finite coefficient ring
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth separated $k$-morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $n\geq1$ and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $\ell^nA=0$. Use ordinary, uncompleted constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Here $\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ means bounded complexes with intrinsically constructible cohomology [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] and finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]; $Rf_{!,A}\dashv f_A^!$ is the constructible adjunction of [sk-prop-sf-existence, sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation]. Write $(-)_A=-\otimes_R^LA$ for scalar extension from $R=\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. The Tate line $A_T(r)$ is the inverse image from the ordinary etale site of $\mu_{\ell^n,T}\otimes_R A_T$ for $r=1$, its tensor powers for $r>0$, $A_T$ for $r=0$, and the dual of $A_T(-r)$ for $r<0$; these are the canonical exponent-independent twists of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], with $K(r)=K\otimes_A^LA_T(r)$. The tensor map in clause (3) means the adjoint transpose of the inverse compact-support projection formula followed by $1_K\otimes\varepsilon_{A_Y}$. At $R$ the orientation of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] is applied with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and level $n$, with the vector-bundle arrow in that diagonal construction given by the inverse of the integration-transposed comparison of [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity]. Then:

1. the relative dualizing complex $\omega_{f,A}=f_A^!A_Y$ has an orientation
   $\omega_{f,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X(d)[2d]$, namely the composite
   $$
   \omega_{f,A}=f_A^!\bigl(((\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_Y)_A\bigr)
   \xleftarrow[\ \sim\ ]{\ c_{\mathbf Z/\ell^n,A}\ }(\omega_{f,\mathbf Z/\ell^n})_A
   \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\bigl((\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_X(d)[2d]\bigr)_A=A_X(d)[2d],
   $$
   where the last map is the extension of scalars of the orientation of
   [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] and $c_{\mathbf Z/\ell^n,A}$ is the
   coefficient comparison of [det-sp-reduction-exceptional];
2. it agrees with the orientation obtained by running the diagonal and
   deformation construction directly with $A$-coefficients;
3. for every $K\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ the composite
   $$
   \gamma_{f,A}(K):\ f_A^*K(d)[2d]\simeq f_A^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_X}A_X(d)[2d]
   \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }f_A^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_X}\omega_{f,A}
   \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }f_A^!K
   $$
   of the inverse orientation and the tensor map is an isomorphism, natural
   in $K$, and it does not depend on the choice of $n$.

proof.text: Put $R=\mathbf Z/\ell^n$. The unital structure map $R\to A$ exists because $\ell^nA=0$. Use the fixed coefficient-independent compactification supplied by [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] for $f$ at both coefficient rings. The unit $R_Y$ is in the bounded constructible finite-Tor category (it is free of rank one in degree zero). Thus [det-sp-reduction-exceptional] gives $c_f:(\omega_{f,R})_A\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{f,A}$. Apply [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] at $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, whose level-$n$ quotient is exactly $R$, to obtain $\theta_{f,R}:\omega_{f,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_X(d)[2d]$. All its scheme hypotheses hold in our explicit separated finite-type setting. Since $\ell$ is invertible on every $k$-scheme here, the Tate clause applies. By the free-line and exact-functor clauses of [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], scalar extension carries this isomorphism to $(\omega_{f,R})_A\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X(d)[2d]$. Set $\theta_{f,A}^{(n)}=(\theta_{f,R})_A c_f^{-1}$. This proves clause (1), with exactly its displayed map and arrow directions.

We compare the three arrows in the diagonal/DNC construction, rather than infer canonicity from the existence of an isomorphism. Put $W=X\times_YX$, with $p_1,p_2$ and $\Delta$. The prime-power diagonal arrow $a_R:C_R(p_1,\Delta)\to\omega_{f,R}$ is the base-change identification of [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change]. Its construction uses the smooth base-change exchange and $p_2\Delta=1_X$. The base-change and pullback coherence in [lem-pur-dnc-coefficient-transport], applied with $g_0=f$, $h=f$, and $g'_0=p_1$ to this square (the base-change clause requires no section of $f$), gives
$$a_A q_{p_1,\Delta}=c_f(a_R)_A.$$
Here $a_A$ is the same specified base-change composite over $A$, not an arbitrary identification. For the actual normal bundle $\pi_N:N_\Delta\to X$, the normalized deformation map $\delta_R:C_R(p_1,\Delta)\to C_R(\pi_N,0_N)$ is [thm-pur-dnc-invariance]. The final equation of [lem-pur-dnc-coefficient-transport] gives
$$\delta_A q_{p_1,\Delta}=q_{\pi_N,0_N}(\delta_R)_A.$$
That lemma identifies $\delta_A$ with the direct normalized construction over $A$, and supplies its uniqueness at $t=1$. The pair is eligible: the diagonal of the smooth separated map $f$ is a closed section of $p_1$ and its actual normal bundle is the rank-$d$ tangent bundle, as stated in [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion]. The geometry, including this bundle, is the same at both coefficient rings. The helper uses [def-pur-dnc-section-family] for that geometric space and its structural maps; its two displayed formulas define the family objects separately at $R$ and $A$, so the fixed-coefficient convention of that definition is respected.

source.place: Proof (2), diagonal and normalized deformation comparisons

proof.text:
The last arrow $\beta_R:C_R(\pi_N,0_N)\to R_X(d)[2d]$ is the zero-section pullback of the canonical vector-bundle orientation [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity]. More precisely, at $R$ the theorem [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity] explicitly specifies its inverse as the transpose of the inverse projection formula followed by integration $t_{\pi_N}$; this is the integration normalization specified in our statement. Over a trivializing open, vector integration is the affine-space counit, and [def-amb-vector-integration] specifies it for every finite ring, including $A$, by these local restrictions and unique gluing. Let $T_D=D_N(d)[2d]$ and let $j_D:T_D\to\omega_{\pi_N,D}$ be the adjoint transpose of $t_{\pi_N,D}$ for $D=R,A$. The specified affine trace of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] is the counit of the ordered affine-space adjunction, so on a trivializing open $j_D$ is the identity in that adjunction's identification $\omega_{p_d,D}=D(d)[2d]$. The chart clause of [det-sp-reduction-exceptional] uses the counit-preserving chart identification, with counit the fibre sum followed by the specified affine-space counit. On a vector-bundle trivializing open the etale coordinate map is the identity, so this fibre sum is the identity and it identifies $c_{\pi_N}$ with the coefficient identification between precisely these affine right adjoints; thus on that open $c_{\pi_N}(j_R)_A=j_A$. To pass from charts to global maps, $c_{\pi_N}(j_R)_A:T_A\to\omega_{\pi_N,A}$ is an isomorphism, since $j_R$ and $c_{\pi_N}$ are isomorphisms. Its target is therefore a locally free rank-one sheaf shifted by $[2d]$, as is its source. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], after removing that common shift both $c_{\pi_N}(j_R)_A$ and $j_A$ are ordinary sheaf morphisms. Their equality on each trivializing open gives equality globally by [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing]. Thus $c_{\pi_N}(j_R)_A=j_A$. The left-hand map is invertible, so $j_A$ is invertible and $j_A^{-1}c_{\pi_N}=(j_R^{-1})_A$. Restrict along the zero section and use the pullback/tensor identification [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and the free-line identification [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. This gives the pullback of the equality between the specified inverse-integration maps just proved. In the pro-etale realization the same equality holds: the finite comparison equivalence [det-ctf-finite-comparison-localizing] respects compact support and pullback, and its tensor comparison is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Consequently the last arrow of the direct $A$-construction satisfies
$$\beta_A q_{\pi_N,0_N}=(\beta_R)_A.$$
The coefficient notation at the zero section is canonical by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. This argument concerns specified integration and its transpose; it never asserts that all isomorphisms of Tate lines coincide.

Proof (2), combining the diagonal/deformation/vector-bundle comparisons; local-to-global identification of the glued prime-power orientation (cf. thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object proof, overlap and gluing steps)

proof.text:
For the tensor formula at arbitrary finite $A$ we use the actual arbitrary-ring theorem, without applying a DVR-quotient theorem outside its domain. Write $v_T=\nu_T^*$. The hypotheses of [det-ctf-finite-comparison-whole] hold: the field is $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $A$ is finite and $\ell$-primary, $\ell$ differs from the characteristic, and both schemes are finite type. By that theorem and [det-ctf-finite-comparison-localizing], $v_T$ is an equivalence from the ordinary etale derived category to the localizing closure in which the adjoint [sk-prop-sf-existence] is defined, compatible with pullback and compact support. The comparison node explicitly identifies finite-discrete constant rings with the pulled-back condensed rings used in the localizing-closure framework; the module categories here are interpreted through that ring-sheaf isomorphism. It is monoidal by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. For etale $H,L$ the natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(v_XH,f_A^!v_YL)
\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_{!,A}v_XH,v_YL)
\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!^{\mathrm{et},A}H,L)
\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(H,f_{\mathrm{et},A}^{\times}L)$$
identify $f_A^!v_YL$ with $v_Xf_{\mathrm{et},A}^{\times}L$, respecting the counit. These are bijections on the whole etale category; the equivalence and right-adjoint uniqueness in [sk-prop-sf-existence] give the indicated natural identification. Apply [thm-asd-smooth-tensor] with $N=\ell^n$. Its Noetherian and compactifiability hypotheses hold: finite-type schemes over $k$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], and the standing scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] supplies a compactification of $f$. This gives the isomorphism $f_{\mathrm{et}}^*L\otimes_A^Lf_{\mathrm{et}}^{\times}A_Y\to f_{\mathrm{et}}^{\times}L$. It identifies with the specified pro-etale tensor map: after the displayed counit identification both transposes are $Rf_!(f^*L\otimes\omega_f)\to L\otimes Rf_!\omega_f\xrightarrow{1\otimes\varepsilon}L$. The projection map is preserved as a specified map: on a proper edge its adjunct is the pullback/tensor comparison followed by the direct-image counit tensored with the identity. Site comparison preserves that counit by its direct-image adjunction comparison and preserves the tensor comparison by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]; the exchange/projection equality of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] identifies the resulting two mates. For an open edge the tensor comparison for extension by zero is the identity on the open and the unique map on the zero sheaves outside it. Composing the proper and open comparisons for the fixed compactification therefore preserves the compact-support projection map. Injectivity of the displayed adjunction bijection identifies the tensor transposes. Thus $f_A^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_{f,A}\to f_A^!K$ is a natural isomorphism. This applies to our $K$, and [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation] gives its stated constructible finite-Tor target.

source.place: Proof (3), tensor formula; arbitrary finite-ring version of the cited orientation-free tensor argument

proof.text: The first arrow in $\gamma_{f,A}(K)$ is tensor reassociation with the Tate line, the second is tensoring the inverse of the isomorphism of Step 1, and the third is the natural tensor isomorphism of Step 5. They are invertible and natural in $K$, so their composite is invertible and natural. To check the choice of exponent, apply Steps 1–4 with any other $n'\geq1$ such that $\ell^{n'}A=0$. Both give exactly $\theta_{f,A}^{\mathrm{dir}}$, the direct diagonal construction at the fixed ring $A$. The Tate identifications for $\ell^n$ and $\ell^{n'}$ are the canonical ones of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], passing through $\ell^{\max(n,n')}$ if needed. The integration normalization also agrees for these two presentations; this requires more than identifying the Tate lines. Put $m=\ell^n$, $M=\ell^{\max(n,n')}$ and $v=M/m$. The exact Kummer sequences of [lem-amb-kummer-any-base] for $M$ and $m$ form a commutative diagram with vertical maps $z\mapsto z^v$ on $\mu_M\to\mu_m$, $z\mapsto z^v$ on the middle $\mathbf G_m$, and the identity on the right $\mathbf G_m$: indeed $(z^v)^m=z^M$. The connecting Chern classes are therefore identified. Concretely, take etale-local $M$-th roots of the transition functions of $\mathcal O(1)$; their $v$-th powers are $m$-th roots of the same functions, and the corresponding boundary cocycles are related by exactly $\mu_M\to\mu_m$. After extension to A this is the canonical Tate identification already cited. In [def-amb-p1-trace], the decomposition has components the unit and that Chern class, so its inverse and the projection defining $t_q$ are identical under this identification. The ordered affine counits in [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] are consequently identical, including the identity for dimension zero. The unique-gluing clause of [def-amb-vector-integration] identifies vector integration at the two exponents. Apply the same argument with $m=\ell^{n'}$. Thus the vector arrow over A is fixed as well. The affine adjunction normalization in [det-sp-reduction-exceptional] and uniqueness of the normalized family map in [lem-pur-dnc-coefficient-transport] now identify all three direct-construction arrows in both presentations. Therefore $\theta_{f,A}^{(n)}=\theta_{f,A}^{(n')}$ and the entire composite $\gamma_{f,A}(K)$ is independent of $n$. This supplies the missing orientation comparison; a coefficient-comparison cocycle by itself would not compare the prime-power orientations.
